reason: The text consistently refers to the Hebrews using collective and national terminology rather than familial language. Key phrases include 'עַמִּי' (my people), 'בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל' (children/sons of Israel), and 'עַם' (people/nation). The text makes explicit national distinctions, particularly the contrast 'בֵּין עַמִּי וּבֵין עַמֶּךָ' (between my people and your people), and establishes territorial boundaries ('אֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן אֲשֶׁר עַמִּי עֹמֵד עָלֶיהָ' - the land of Goshen where my people stands). While their relationship to Yahweh is mentioned, they are primarily identified as a distinct national collective with geographical territory, not merely as a family group or religious followers.
